battle.name: 盧公暹起義
battle.theater: 河南道黎陽津與渤海郡滄州
battle.brief: 大業十二年（616）春，隋煬帝自江都北上，護駕的鐵勒騎兵在黎陽因缺糧反叛，渠帥盧公暹、司王金士才聚眾攻破滄州，隋廷遣將討平。卡面這件羅馬重步兵從未到過中國，它標示的是另一種打仗的方式：靠國家長期供養、靠補充兵源與補給線維持的重裝步兵體系。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 大業十二年（616）的衝突有兩個交戰主體：其一是隋朝中央及其在河北道、河南道一線的駐軍，其二是以盧公暹、司王金士才為首、由護駕鐵勒騎兵骨幹組成的叛軍。隋廷這一邊的指揮體系正在瓦解：尚書省兵部早已只剩符印與軍籍之權，調兵靠行軍總管、總管、判官逐級傳令，郡縣以太守、令領郡兵縣兵應敵；大業年間三次征高句麗把府兵抽空，募兵、逃戶與降附部眾被混編充數，兵員的裝備與操練參差不齊。黎陽與滄州一線的守備，本地靠郡兵與屯田戍卒，外線靠護駕的鐵勒騎兵，兩者之間靠永濟渠與黃河水運聯繫。叛軍這一邊的構成更特殊：主力是數萬鐵勒騎兵，渠帥卻是高句麗降人盧公暹與司王金士才；這支人馬既隸屬隋朝的護駕序列，又握有馬匹、機動力與劫掠的能力，隨時可以脫離朝廷自立。第三方同樣在場：北面是契丹與靺鞨的游騎，屢次越塞抄掠；東北的高句麗收留了叛首，與隋廷形成外交糾葛；同一年在靈丘有翟松柏起事，在涿郡一線有羅藝脫離朝廷，在漳州有操師乞起兵，四方亂局同年並發，而中樞的注意力仍繫在遼東與江都之間的巡幸上。
countriesEn: The conflict of 616 had two principals: the Sui court together with the troops it still held along the Hebei and Henan circuits, and the rebel host built around the escorting Huihu cavalry under the banner of Lu Gongxian and Siwang Jin Shicai. On the Sui side the command system was coming apart. Under the Ministry of War only the tallies and the personnel rolls retained any real authority; troops were moved by travelling army commissioners, commandants and registrars passing orders down the chain; and the prefectures and counties answered with commandery and county levies under their administrators. The three campaigns against Goguryeo had drained the fubing establishment hollow, so that hired soldiers, runaways and surrendered groups were mixed into the ranks to make up the numbers, and the equipment and drill of the men were uneven. The defence of the Liyang and Cangzhou line rested on the commandery levies and the military-farm settlers inside the country, and on the escorting Huihu cavalry outside it, and the two were joined by the Yongji Canal and the water traffic of the Yellow River. The composition of the rebel side was more unusual still. The main body was a Huihu cavalry numbering tens of thousands, but the commanders in its ranks were two men from Goguryeo who had come over to the Sui; the force was therefore at once part of the court's escort establishment and in possession of the horses, the mobility and the means to plunder, and it could detach itself from the throne at any moment. Third parties were present as well. To the north the riders of the Khitan and the Mohe crossed the frontier again and again to carry off cattle. To the northeast Goguryeo took in the rebel leaders and became entangled with the Sui in diplomacy. And in the same year there was the rising of Zhai Songbai at Lingqiu, the break of Luo Yi from the court in the Zuo commandery line, and the rising of Cao Shiqi at Zhangzhou, so that disorder flared in several quarters at once, while the centre of government still fixed its attention on Liaodong and on the court's movements between Jiangdu and Luoyang.
people: 盧公暹是這場叛亂的旗幟人物。舊史記他與司王金士才同為高句麗人，先降於隋而受官，後在護駕的鐵勒騎兵中任渠帥；司王本是北方王號，金是同姓，兩人各掌一翼之眾，既熟習騎兵的部伍與騎射，又在隋廷的軍序中握有實權。他們最關鍵的一步，是在缺糧與饑荒之中說服鐵勒眾叛離朝廷：先藉口徵糧，殺傷監押的隋官，然後裹挾騎兵奪取州縣的倉廩，一路由黎陽打到滄州。隋煬帝楊廣是這一端的最高決策者，他往返於江都、洛陽與涿郡之間巡行，對河北的處置只能以詔書徵兵徵糧、遣使責問，實際指揮落在行軍總管與各州刺史手上。直接經手的隋將，舊史所載互有出入：一說以左翊衛大將軍韋雲起為主，韋雲起正是招致鐵勒、率眾護駕的那位將領，也是滄州一線的守將；一說以武衛大將軍樊子略為討平之役的主將。東北方面，高句麗王收納公暹與士才為客將，隋使一到便遣使上表請罪而不肯交人，這段交涉一直拖到隋亡之後。同期在別處起兵的翟松柏、操師乞、李淵、竇建德，以及在瓦崗寨與張須陀之間周旋的官軍，都是這條亂世因果鏈上的角色；張須陀的敗亡與護駕兵變同屬一條線的下游，而其後不滿一年，江都兵變、隋室覆亡。
peopleEn: Lu Gongxian is the figurehead of the rising. The old histories record him and Siwang Jin Shicai as men of Goguryeo who had first come over to the Sui and been given office, and who afterwards held the rank of quashuai, the commanders of the tribal wings, in the escorting Huihu cavalry. Siwang was in origin a northern princely title and Jin was the surname of the house, so the two of them each commanded a wing of the host, being at once practised in the drill and the mounted archery of the horse and holding real authority in the military order of the Sui. Their decisive step was to persuade the Huihu to break away from the court at a moment of want and famine: first, on the pretext of drawing grain, they killed the Sui officers who kept the men, then they carried the cavalry off with the stores of the prefectures and counties, and struck from Liyang as far as Cangzhou. Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang, was the highest decision-maker at the other end of the affair. He was travelling between Jiangdu, Luoyang and Zhuojun, and all he could do for the north was to issue edicts calling up men and grain and to send envoys to upbraid; the actual command lay with the travelling army commissioners and the prefectural governors. The Sui officers actually engaged are recorded inconsistently: one account makes the left guard commander Wei Yunqi the chief, and Wei Yunqi was precisely the man who had raised the Huihu and led them as escort, and the governor on the Cangzhou line; another makes the guard commander Fan Zilue the commander of the force that put the rising down. In the northeast the king of Goguryeo took in Gongxian and Shicai and gave them the rank of guest generals; when the Sui envoy arrived he sent back a memorial of apology but would not surrender the men, and this business dragged on until after the fall of the Sui. Those who rose elsewhere at the same time, Zhai Songbai, Cao Shiqi, Li Yuan and Dou Jiande, together with the court troops manoeuvring between the Wagang stronghold and Zhang Xuetuo, were all players on the same chain of cause and effect. The defeat of Zhang Xuetuo and the mutiny of the escort lie further down the same line, and less than a year after them came the mutiny at Jiangdu and the end of the Sui house.
kits: 先說清楚：卡面這件羅馬重步兵從來沒有到過中國，黎陽與滄州的城頭上不會出現它。它代表的是一套可以與隋軍對照的裝備與體系。羅馬重步兵的骨架是三件東西：分段鎧甲，鐵片寬約八公分、高約四公分，成串披掛，全副約九公斤；大方盾，弧形，半人高，約一公尺一至一公尺二，寬約六十至八十公分，重量十餘公斤；一柄約六十公分長、約一公斤重的短劍。遠距用標槍，槍身約兩米，鐵製標槍頭約六十至七十公分，擲出可達三十米以上；兩翼與後隊是持短矛的輕裝兵。中國這一邊與之對位的，是隋軍的環首刀、直刃刀、長槊與大盾，遠射用臂弩與床弩，弩有弩機、望山與矢道，騎兵用馬槊與騎射。護駕的鐵勒騎兵本身是另一種重裝騎兵，以標槍與彎刀見長，馬政與弓矢齊備，靠的是成群的機動力而不是攻城器械。攻城一端的器具則是雲梯、撞車、巢車與火箭；黎陽津是黃河與永濟渠交會的渡口，守方靠舟船、浮橋與壘壁，攻方靠騎兵衝鋒後的近身衝撞與火攻。除兵器之外還有馬匹、糧秣與運輸：羅馬軍團的糧道靠每日五羅馬里、約七點四公里一營的推進與營地開墾維繫，隋軍在河北的糧道則靠永濟渠漕運與郡縣徵發，二者都受制於線的長短這件事。
kitsEn: To be clear at the start: the Roman legionary on this card never came to China, and it would not have appeared on the towers of Liyang or Cangzhou. What it stands for is an equipment system and a way of fighting that can be set against the Sui army. The skeleton of a Roman heavy infantryman is three things: segmented plate armour, with iron bands about eight centimetres wide and four centimetres high, hung in overlapping courses and weighing roughly nine kilogrammes the whole set; the large curved shield, semicircular in shape, half a man's height, about one metre ten to one metre twenty, sixty to eighty centimetres across and something over ten kilogrammes in weight; and a short sword about sixty centimetres long and about a kilogramme in weight. At range he used the javelin, shaft about two metres, with an iron shank of sixty to seventy centimetres that could be thrown thirty metres or more, while the flanks and the rear were carried by light troops with short spears. The Chinese counterpart in the same slots is the Sui ring-pommel dao, the straight dao, the long spear and the large shield, with the handheld crossbow and the heavy crossbow for shooting; the crossbow has its trigger mechanism, its sight and its groove, and the horse carried the mounted spear and the bow. The escorting Huihu cavalry were themselves a form of heavy cavalry, famous for the javelin and the curved sabre, with a full horse administration and a complete supply of arrows; their strength lay in massed mobility rather than in siege engines. The apparatus of an assault had its own names on the Sui side: scaling ladders, battering rams, siege towers and fire arrows. Liyangjin was the crossing where the Yellow River met the Yongji Canal, and the defenders relied on boats, on floating bridges and on ramparts, while the attackers relied on the shock of cavalry followed by close assault and by fire. Beyond the weapons there were the horses, the grain and the transport: the Roman grain road was held together by the daily advance of about five Roman miles, some seven and a half kilometres, and by the cultivation of the camp land, whereas the Sui grain road in the north ran on the freight of the Yongji Canal and on requisition from the commanderies; both were governed in the end by the length of the line.
tactics: 叛軍的作戰樣式是一場以奪糧為先的機動作戰。鐵勒騎兵在飢餓之中首先要做的是搶糧：他們沒有攻城器械，也不打算攻堅城，而是沿黃河與永濟渠的水道快速推進，攻掠沿線的州縣與倉廩，憑騎兵的速度把每一處能吃的東西帶走，同時把徵發來的郡兵與縣兵裹挾進來。滄州是渤海郡的治所所在，郡兵本應據城固守，但守備一旦瓦解，叛軍便能以騎兵環城的辦法接管城中的府庫與器械。隋軍這一端的應對分兩步：先以洛陽與涿郡為基地，遣行軍總管率各郡之兵沿永濟渠兩側搜索，試圖切斷叛軍與散在鄉里的鐵勒騎兵之間的聯繫；再以騎兵與弩陣在叛軍回援與轉移的途中截擊，迫其放棄攻城與劫掠，返回黎陽一線決戰。這裡可以看出當時隋軍的真實狀態：府兵制已名存實亡，能作戰的多是臨時徵發與降附混編的部隊，攻城靠撞車與雲梯這些老器械，野戰靠騎兵與弩，而全軍最缺的不是武器，是能持續供應的糧秣與統一指揮的指揮系統。卡面這件羅馬重步兵所代表的恰好是反面：羅馬的交替掩護縱隊要求嚴格的輪換與營地紀律，每日扎營、每日挖掘壕溝、每日推進固定里程，士卒的裝備由國家長期供應，這套東西在隋廷的護駕序列裡根本不存在；叛軍之所以能在一夜之間把一支隊伍變成叛兵，靠的正是這支隊伍從來沒有被國家真正管住。
tacticsEn: The manner of the rising was a mobile operation whose first object was to seize grain. Hungry, the Huihu cavalry did what hungry cavalry do: they had no siege engines and no intention of assaulting a walled city, and so they moved fast along the water routes of the Yellow River and the Yongji Canal, raiding the prefectures, counties and granaries on the way, carrying off with them whatever could be eaten, and drawing in the commandery and county levies that had been conscripted. Cangzhou was the seat of the commandery of Bohai, where the levies should have held the city, but once the defence collapsed the rebels could take the city from the outside with cavalry and take over the stores and the ordnance within it. The Sui response worked in two steps. First, basing themselves on Luoyang and on Zhuojun, the travelling army commissioners were sent out with the levies of the several commanderies to search along both banks of the Yongji Canal, in the hope of cutting the rebels off from the Huihu riders scattered over the countryside. Then mounted troops and crossbow formations were used to intercept the rebels as they came back to relieve or to shift position, in the hope of forcing them to give up the towns and the plunder and to return towards Liyang for a decisive engagement. The real condition of the Sui army shows through here: the fubing system existed in name only, the troops that could really fight were temporary levies mixed with surrendered groups, a siege was carried with rams and ladders of an older pattern, a field action with cavalry and crossbows, and what the army lacked above all was not weapons but the grain to feed itself and a command system that could direct it. The Roman legionary on the card stands for the opposite. The relieving line of the Roman army demanded strict rotation and strict camp discipline: a camp every night, a ditch dug every night, a fixed day's march every day, and the equipment of the men was fed and replaced over long service. None of that existed in the escort establishment of the Sui court. And that is precisely why a body of troops could become a body of rebels within a single night: it was because that body had never really been held by the state.
data: 可核的數字有幾組。時間：事繫大業十二年（616），史家有繫於同年四月者，亦有繫於季夏者，卡面取616年。兵員：隋廷三次征高句麗，第一次舉兵約一百一十三萬，第二次約六十萬，第三次約三十萬，役後士卒死亡以十數萬計，府兵在十年之間被抽空；護駕鐵勒騎兵的數目在史書中諸說並存，有作三萬餘者，有作數十萬者，較可信者當取少數一說。水道：永濟渠自洛陽東北至涿郡，全長二千餘里，渠寬四十步；黎陽津在黃河與永濟渠交會處，離洛陽二百餘里，至涿郡一千餘里，隋煬帝自江都北上，所循的就是這條線，一里約合今半公里。器械：羅馬方面，軍團約五千至五千五百人，連輔助兵近一萬，營為六個百人隊所組成，百人隊八十人，最小的八人小組八人；標槍擲出可達三十米以上，短劍約六十公分、約一公斤，大盾高約一公尺一至一公尺二，分段鎧甲約九公斤；軍隊每日行軍約五羅馬里即七點四公里，每兵每日配給穀物約一斗，約零點九公斤，並加少量豆類與醋酒，鹽按月發放。編年上的對照：隋亡於618年，盧公暹等出奔高句麗的記錄在隋末唐初的史書中延續到唐武德年間，隋廷與高句麗就交人與否的交涉亦見於此後數年的記載。
dataEn: There are several groups of figures that can be vouched for. On time: the affair belongs to the twelfth year of Daye under Emperor Yang of Sui, that is 616; some historians place it in the fourth month of that year and others in high summer, and the card takes 616. On numbers of men: the Sui court campaigned against Goguryeo three times, raising about one million one hundred and thirty thousand men the first time, about six hundred thousand the second and about three hundred thousand the third, and counting the dead among the soldiers in the tens of thousands afterwards, so that the fubing establishment was emptied within a decade; the size of the Huihu escort is given inconsistently in the histories, at three tens of thousands in one place and at tens of thousands in another, and the smaller figure is the more credible. On the water route: the Yongji Canal ran from Luoyang in the north-east to Zhuojun, over two thousand li in length and forty paces in width; Liyangjin lay where the Yellow River met that canal, some two hundred-odd li from Luoyang and some thousand-odd li from Zhuojun, and it was along this line that Emperor Yang travelled north from Jiangdu, a li being about half a kilometre to-day. On the weapons: for the Romans, a legion numbered about five to five and a half thousand men, nearly ten thousand with the auxiliaries, was made up of ten cohorts of six centuries, a century being eighty men and the smallest unit a contubernium of eight; the javelin was thrown thirty metres or more, the short sword was about sixty centimetres and about a kilogramme, the large shield about one metre ten to one metre twenty high, the segmented armour about nine kilogrammes; the army marched about five Roman miles, some seven and a half kilometres, a day, and each man was issued about a modius of grain, roughly zero point nine kilogramme, with a little pulse and vinegar or wine, and salt was issued by the month. On the chronology: the Sui fell in 618, and the record of Lu Gongxian and his companion fleeing to Goguryeo runs on into the histories of the Sui-Tang transition and into the Wude years of the Tang, which also carry the exchanges between the Sui court and Goguryeo over whether the men would be given up.
cause: 直接的原因很單純：護駕的鐵勒騎兵在黎陽斷糧，而河南正遇饑荒，郡縣無法供應軍需，隋廷的處置又急又硬。鐵勒是外族附屬的徵召兵，裝備與糧餉都靠中央臨時接濟，饑荒一來，徵發無以為繼，於是饑餓本身成了最好的號召。盧公暹與司王金士才這兩個高句麗降人正是在這個節點上把饑餓變成了叛亂的理由：他們殺死監押的隋官，奪了倉廩，把一支飢餓的騎兵變成自己的部眾。深一層的原因是隋朝整個軍隊體系的崩壞。府兵在開皇年間尚有定制，三次征高句麗之後府兵被抽空，國家改用募兵與降附部眾充數，兵不習戰，糧餉無常，邊軍與護駕兵同中央的關係只剩一紙徵調；同時隋煬帝把大量物資與注意力放在遼東與江都的巡幸上，河南、冀北一線的郡縣既要供京師又要供軍隊，地方與中央的裂痕越拉越大。附屬部眾的地位也是關鍵：鐵勒在隋的體系裡是客軍，歸降的高句麗人做渠帥，於是中央既依賴他們又防備他們，朝廷的每一次加糧、每一道命令都可能成為叛亂的觸發點。606年以後讖言與歌謠在河北、山東傳播，講的是劉氏當有天下，人心早已不耐；616年發生在黎陽的這場兵變，正是這種不耐與飢餓在最薄弱的一個環節上爆開。
causeEn: The immediate cause was plain enough. The escorting Huihu cavalry ran out of grain at Liyang, Henan was in the grip of a famine, the commanderies could not supply the army, and the court's handling of the case was both hurried and harsh. The Huihu were foreign auxiliaries levied for the occasion, and both their equipment and their rations depended on the centre making provision for them at the moment; once the famine came and the requisitions dried up, hunger itself became the best possible summons. Lu Gongxian and Siwang Jin Shicai, the two men who had come over from Goguryeo, turned hunger into a reason for revolt at precisely this point: they killed the Sui officers who kept the men, seized the granaries, and turned a hungry cavalry into their own retainers. The deeper cause is the collapse of the Sui military system as a whole. The fubing had had a regular shape in the Kaihuang years, and after the three campaigns against Goguryeo it was hollow, so that the state made up its numbers with hired soldiers and surrendered groups, who had little drill and no settled pay; the relation between the frontier and escort troops and the centre came down to a single paper call. At the same time Emperor Yang was spending the material resources and the attention of the state on Liaodong and on the tours of Jiangdu, and the commanderies of Henan and of northern Ji had to feed the capital and feed the army at once, so the rift between the provinces and the centre widened steadily. The standing of the affiliated peoples was decisive in its own way. Within the Sui system the Huihu were a guest force, commanded by men who had surrendered from Goguryeo, so that the court both relied on them and watched them, and every ration it added and every order it issued was a possible trigger of revolt. From 606 onward prophecies and songs telling that a house surnamed Liu would hold the realm had been passing through Hebei and Shandong, and the mood of the people had long ceased to endure. The mutiny at Liyang in 616 was that weariness and that hunger bursting at the weakest point in the chain.
impact: 這場起事的第一層影響在隋朝的信用：它讓隋朝第一次出現護駕的兵反過來打朝廷的局面，而且發生在皇帝自己的行程上。此後朝廷對護駕與客軍的政策更趨嚴控與猜忌，附屬部眾的編制與糧餉由寬轉緊，北方邊軍與外族部眾之間的信任進一步受損。第二層影響在東北：高句麗收留盧公暹與司王金士才並以客將待之，隋使來索人不予，雙方在遼東與朝鮮半島一線的外交摩擦延續多年；這條線在隋亡之後仍在，619年唐廷遣使赴高句麗交涉叛將的下落，同一議題的拉鋸一直延續到唐初，為唐初的東北經營留下一個難題。第三層影響在中原亂局的次序上：616年前後，靈丘的翟松柏、黎陽與滄州一線的盧公暹、幽州的羅藝、漳州的操師乞幾乎同年並起，而瓦崗、張須陀、竇建德、李淵各據一方，隋朝已無力逐一心平；一年後江都兵變、隋室覆亡，這些起義在事後的回望裡便成了同一條崩解曲線上的幾個點。第四層在後世的記錄方式上：正史只留下寥寥數語，而這場由一支饑餓騎兵引發的叛亂，卻說明了一個常被忽略的道理——國家的戰力不只在兵員數目，更在於它能不能持續養住、編整與指揮一支外來隊伍。
impactEn: The first layer of consequence lies in the credit of the Sui state: the rising produced the first occasion on which the troops escorting the emperor turned and fought the court, and it happened on the emperor's own road. The court's policy towards escorts and guest troops grew stricter and more suspicious afterwards, the organisation and the rations of affiliated peoples were tightened, and the trust between the northern frontier forces and the foreign contingents was damaged further. The second layer lies in the northeast. Goguryeo took in Lu Gongxian and Siwang Jin Shicai and gave them the rank of guest generals; the Sui envoys came to ask for the men and were refused; and the diplomatic friction between the two along the Liaodong and peninsula lines ran on for years. The thread did not end with the Sui: in 619 the Tang court sent envoys to Goguryeo over the whereabouts of the rebel leaders, and the same business was still being pulled and hauled in the early Tang, leaving the Tang's handling of the northeast a standing difficulty. The third layer lies in the order of the disorder in the central plains. Around 616 the rising of Zhai Songbai at Lingqiu, the rising of Lu Gongxian on the Liyang and Cangzhou line, the break of Luo Yi at Youzhou and the rising of Cao Shiqi at Zhangzhou all came in the same year, while the Wagang band, Zhang Xuetuo, Dou Jiande and Li Yuan each held a quarter of the country, and the Sui no longer had the strength to put them down one by one; a year later came the mutiny at Jiangdu and the end of the Sui house, and in the rear view these risings are only several points on a single curve of dissolution. The fourth layer lies in how the affair was recorded afterwards. The official histories preserve a few lines and no more, and yet a mutiny set off by a hungry cavalry says something that is habitually overlooked: the fighting power of a state is not in the number of men it has, but in whether it can keep, organise and command a foreign contingent over time.
result: 起事在短時間內是成功的：叛軍奪了黎陽的倉廩，攻破滄州，一度把渤海郡與永濟渠沿線的漕運與徵發攔腰截斷，隋煬帝的北上行程被迫走走停停；但它終究只是一場饑荒引發的軍事騷亂，沒有土地、沒有政權、也沒有能持續供給的後方。隋廷的討伐軍在洛陽與涿郡兩端部署，切斷叛軍與鐵勒騎兵的聯繫，最終在黎陽、滄州一線把它壓了下去；叛眾被平定，盧公暹與司王金士才拋下部眾，北走高句麗。高句麗王收留二人、授以客將之號，隋使來責問便遣使上表請罪而不肯交人，隋廷不接受，這件事就這樣拖到隋亡以後。從全局看，這場叛亂的直接結果是隋朝在河南、河北一線的軍政秩序加速瓦解：郡縣不再能單獨應敵，客軍不再能被信任，朝廷的詔令與實際控制力脫節。也正因如此，一年之後的江都兵變、618年的隋亡以及隨後的群雄割據，並不是突然而來。要說記載有限之處：起義的確切日期、雙方兵數、交戰地點與勝負細節，正史與《資治通鑑》都只留片段，過程多靠後人推想；而卡面那件羅馬重步兵自不曾出現在黎陽，它能提示的只有一點——羅馬靠國家供養、靠補充兵源與補給線維持的重步兵體系，與一支靠臨時徵召、靠搶糧維生的騎兵之間，隔著的正是制度，而不是勇敢。
resultEn: For a short time the rising was a success. The rebels took the stores at Liyang, broke into Cangzhou, and for a while cut the freight and the requisitions of the Bohai commandery and the Yongji Canal across the middle, so that the emperor's northward journey was interrupted and delayed. But in the end it was only a military disturbance born of famine: it had no land, no government and no rear from which it could be supplied. The Sui deployed its punitive force from the two ends of the line, from Luoyang and from Zhuojun, and worked to cut the rebels off from the Huihu riders, and in the end it pressed the rising down on the Liyang and Cangzhou line. The rebel bands were dispersed, and Lu Gongxian and Siwang Jin Shicai abandoned their men and went north to Goguryeo. The king of Goguryeo received the two of them and gave them the rank of guest generals; when the Sui envoys came to upbraid he sent a memorial of apology but would not give the men up; the court would not accept that, and so the business dragged on until after the fall of the Sui. Seen in the wider view, the immediate result of the rising was an acceleration of the breakdown of the Sui military and civil order along the Henan and Hebei lines: the commanderies could no longer meet an enemy on their own, the guest troops could no longer be trusted, and the edicts of the court had come adrift from its actual control. It is for that reason that the mutiny at Jiangdu a year later, the end of the Sui in 618 and the wars of the successor states were not a sudden turn. As to what the record does not carry: the exact date of the rising, the numbers on either side, the places of fighting and the detail of who won and lost survive only in fragments in the official histories and in the Comprehensive Mirror, and the course of it has largely to be reconstructed. And the Roman legionary on the card never stood at Liyang, so the only thing it can suggest is this: between a heavy infantry system sustained by the state, by the renewal of men and by a supply line, and a cavalry that was levied for the occasion and lived on what it could seize, the distance is one of institutions, not of courage.
